fix_commit.message: Fix instances of potential buffer overflow caused by loading the contents of a stat4 table with an absurd number of samples in a 32-bit build. Bug [bugs:/info/2026-06-16T11:30:52Z | 2026-06-16T11:30:52Z].
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: 32-bit integer overflow in stat4 allocation size calculation
findings.message: In loadStatTbl() in src/analyze.c, the buffer size for Index.aSample[] is computed using 32-bit arithmetic on 32-bit builds. sizeof(IndexSample) returns size_t (32-bit on 32-bit platforms) and nSample is int (32-bit). Their product, e.g. ROUND8(sizeof(IndexSample) * nSample), is evaluated entirely in 32-bit arithmetic before being assigned to i64 nByte. If nSample is sufficiently large (e.g., > ~2^27 when sizeof(IndexSample) ~= 32), the multiplication wraps around to a small or zero value. sqlite3DbMallocZero() then allocates an undersized buffer, and subsequent writes of the stat4 sample data overflow the heap allocation.
findings.suggestion: Use sizeof64() instead of sizeof() when multiplying by a potentially large count to ensure 64-bit arithmetic is used even on 32-bit builds. The fix introduced the macro sizeof64(X) = (sqlite3_int64)sizeof(X) and applied it to all four sizeof() calls in the allocation size computation.

ground_truth.root_cause: sizeof() returns size_t, which is 32-bit on 32-bit platforms. When combined with a 32-bit int operand (nSample), the multiplication is computed in 32-bit arithmetic before assignment to a wider type. Although nByte was widened to i64 by a prior partial fix (fe15ed4342), the overflow in the sub-expression sizeof(IndexSample) * nSample already occurs before the value is stored. The fix introduces sizeof64() which returns sqlite3_int64, forcing 64-bit arithmetic throughout.
